articles.title: King Charles Reportedly Told Princess Diana’s Brother “We’ll Forget Her Soon” Just Days After Her Death
articles.summary: Charles Spencer’s new memoir Swan Song is set to be explosive for the royal family.
articles.body:
"Hearst Magazines and Yahoo may earn commission or revenue on some items through these links."

Princess Diana's brother's new memoir, Swan Song , comes out next week, but new revelations published in the Daily Mail today are already shocking. Namely, days after Princess Diana's death, then-Prince Charles reportedly told Charles Spencer "rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough."

The two men had a fight over the decision to have Princes William and Harry, then 15 and 12, walk in the funeral procession for their mother . The Mail notes , "The Earl says he insisted to the then Prince of Wales that Diana would not have wanted her young sons to endure such a public ordeal. It is claimed Charles then questioned the Spencer family's sense of duty before saying his ex-wife, whose death sparked a global outpouring of grief, would soon be forgotten."

"Prince Charles continued his stream of anger, without me interrupting. Then he stopped," Spencer reportedly writes in Swan Song . 'I assumed the pause signalled an effort to bring himself under control, but then he unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death. 'Rest assured,' he hissed, 'we'll forget her soon enough!'"

A Buckingham Palace spokesperson said in reaction, "While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss."

Prince Philip was reportedly instrumental in the decision to have the young boys walk in the funereal cortège. "I seem to remember him saying that in fact, it was a question of, 'If you'll do it, I'll do it,'" Princess Anne said in 2021 after her Philip's death. "And that was him as a grandfather saying to them, 'If you want me to be there, if that's what you want to do and if you want me to be there, I will be there.'"

Prince William, too, said in Diana: 7 Days , a BBC documentary, "It wasn't an easy decision, and it was a collective family decision to do that." Prince Harry later said he thinks it was the wrong choice. "I don't think any child should be asked to do that, under any circumstances. I don't think it would happen today," he said in 2017.

Scheduled for release on September 22, 2026, Swan Song: Diana, My Sister will cover Diana's life through her brother's eyes. "As with my eulogy, I want to speak on Diana's behalf and do so in an openly positive way," Spencer said in a statement when the book was announced last month . "I hope this book will be of interest to the many who still cherish the memory of Diana when she was alive, and I would be delighted if those too young to remember her in her heyday feel—after reading this—that they 'get' who she really was: a one-off, dynamic character, full of love, charisma and self-doubt, who gave life a hell of a go, and left the world a far better place, despite exiting the stage while still so young."

The Mail reveals that Swan Song "includes a string of further extraordinary claims about Diana's failed marriage to King Charles and the tumultuous aftermath of her tragic death in a car crash in Paris in 1997." Four copies of the book were stolen yesterday in the Netherlands .

articles.title: Quote of the day by Ellen DeGeneres: 'It was so important for me to lose everything...I found out what the most important thing...to be true to yourself,' a powerful life lesson explaining the worth of self-acceptance
articles.summary: Discover Ellen DeGeneres' inspiring quote on the importance of being true to yourself and the courage it takes to accept loss and embrace self-acceptance. A must-read for personal growth!
articles.body: Ellen DeGeneres is one of Hollywood's most beloved stars, known for her vibrant personality. In addition to her unmatched charm, she has a treasure of wisdom that has been inspiring generations for years. For instance, once, with her words, Ellen DeGeneres highlighted how the toughest journey for anyone is judged not by the distance travelled, but by the paths covered. Sometimes, it is important to lose everything, to find what matters the most: to find your true self.Today's quote of the day by Ellen DeGeneres reads: 'It was so important for me to lose everything because I found out what the most important thing is, is to be true to yourself. Ultimately, that’s what’s gotten me to this place. I don’t live in fear. I’m free. I have no secrets, and I know I’ll always be okay because no matter what, I know who I am.'What is the meaning of Ellen DeGeneres’ quote?When Ellen shared these words, she was not talking about a small disappointment or an ordinary career setback. She was reflecting on a period when coming out publicly as gay had a serious impact on her career. Her sitcom was cancelled, work became difficult to find and, as she explained in the speech, she spent years wondering what would happen next.The quote came during DeGeneres’ 2009 commencement address at Tulane University, where she spoke to the university’s 'Katrina class.' Tulane’s own archive identifies the speech and preserves the line about losing everything and discovering the importance of being true to yourself.What makes the quote powerful is that DeGeneres does not describe losing everything as something she wishes had never happened. Looking back, she says it helped her understand herself more clearly.At the heart of the quote is a fairly simple idea: knowing who you are can become more important than holding on to what you have. That sounds straightforward, but it can be surprisingly difficult in real life.Careers, relationships, popularity and other people's opinions can become tied to the way we see ourselves. When one of those things disappears, it can feel as though we have lost a part of ourselves too.DeGeneres’ experience suggests another way of looking at it. Losing something can sometimes force you to separate your identity from the role you were playing.Her words are not saying that loss is automatically good or that difficult experiences should be romanticised. They are about what can happen afterwards. Once the noise dies down, a person may have a better idea of what they actually believe, want and value.DeGeneres’ story also shows that courage does not always feel courageous while you are living through it. In her Tulane speech, she recalled being afraid that coming out could end her career. She said that it did: her sitcom was cancelled and she went without offers for years. That period clearly came with anger, sadness and uncertainty.Yet she also described discovering a sense of purpose during that time. She received letters from young people who said her decision had affected them, and she began to see that what had happened was bigger than her career.That does not erase how difficult the period was. But it shows how a decision that initially looks like a loss can sometimes take on a different meaning with time.Being yourself sounds easy until there is something at stake. It can be difficult to disagree with people when you are worried about disappointing them. It can be difficult to leave a situation that looks perfect from the outside. It can be difficult to admit that the version of yourself everyone else knows is not the person you actually want to be. Sometimes the pressure is obvious. Other times, it is much quieter.A person may choose a career because their family expects it. Someone might stay in a relationship because they are afraid of starting over. Another person may hide an opinion because they do not want to be judged.None of these choices automatically means someone is living a false life. People make compromises for all kinds of reasons. But DeGeneres’ quote raises an important question: how much of your life is actually being decided by you?Why is Ellen DeGeneres’ quote relevant today?Social media makes it easy to compare careers, relationships, appearances and lifestyles. People can spend a lot of time trying to look successful while privately wondering whether the life they are showing actually feels right. DeGeneres’ words offer a different measure of success.It is not simply about how many people know your name, how impressive your career looks or how much you have managed to collect. It is also about whether you can live with yourself when nobody is watching.That is probably the hardest part of being true to yourself. There is no audience to impress and no applause at the end of it.Sometimes, it is simply about knowing that the decisions you are making belong to you.Ellen DeGeneres’ Journey From New Orleans to Television StardomLong before she became one of television's most recognisable hosts, Ellen DeGeneres was a young woman growing up in the New Orleans area and trying to figure out what she wanted to do.She worked a string of jobs after leaving school and eventually turned toward stand-up comedy. By 1981, she was performing regularly and working as an emcee at Clyde’s Comedy Club in New Orleans. The following year, she won Showtime’s “Funniest Person in America” competition, giving her career a major push.Her breakthrough continued when she appeared on The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson in 1986. Carson invited her to sit beside him after her performance, something that was a significant moment for a young comedian trying to establish herself.Television success followed. Her sitcom Ellen eventually became a major part of her career, but in 1997, DeGeneres publicly came out as gay, both as herself and through her television character. The decision was groundbreaking, but it also came with a professional cost. The show ended the following year, and DeGeneres later spoke openly about the period in which work almost disappeared.Years later, she returned to daytime television with The Ellen DeGeneres Show, which premiered in 2003 and became a major success.By the time she stood at the Tulane commencement podium in 2009, she had already experienced both sides of the story she was telling the graduating class: the thrill of success and the fear of losing it. That is what makes the quote feel different from a generic motivational line.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Hannah Einbinder's brutal message to Ed Sheeran fuels growing celebrity revolt over Macklemore tour drama
articles.summary: Hannah Einbinder roasted Ed Sheeran on Instagram after Macklemore was dropped from the "Loop Tour" over his onstage pro-Palestine comments..
articles.body: Hannah Einbinder has taken aim at Ed Sheeran amid the growing backlash over Macklemore’s removal from the singer’s U.S. tour. The "Hacks" star criticized Sheeran on Instagram, joking that she was speaking "as a ginger" before wishing him an especially painful sunburn. "Ed Sheeran i say this as a ginger. i hope you get a REALLY bad sun burn the kind on the back of your entire body where it hurts to lie down or walk or sit." MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE Her post came after Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran’s "Loop Tour" following onstage comments supporting Palestine. Einbinder was among several celebrities to publicly call out Sheeran, who addressed the controversy in a lengthy statement posted Tuesday. "Macklemore asked to join my tour last year and I agreed, because I respect him as an artist," Sheeran wrote on social media. "As with all my support acts, I agree that they play a setlist of their choosing." On Monday, Macklemore had claimed that Sheeran told him Robert Kraft, the owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, had rallied other stadium owners to oppose allowing the rapper to perform. According to his account, the venues allegedly gave Sheeran an ultimatum: "if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues." Sheeran’s statement offered a different account of the events, saying that after Macklemore’s performances at his New Jersey shows, venues scheduled for upcoming tour dates told organizers they would pull the shows if Macklemore remained on the lineup. "After Macklemore’s performances at my New Jersey shows, venues on my upcoming tour dates communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting," Sheeran wrote. "I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said. I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft. I was also involved in direct talks with promoters along with activists on both sides to try and find a mutual resolution for all, but the venue’s and promoter’s decision was final." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Sheeran said he has deliberately avoided using his professional platform for politics because his audience includes young people and children from diverse backgrounds. Sheeran said concertgoers attend his shows expecting "a place of safety and sanctuary" rather than a political forum. "There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics – my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds," he wrote. "Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace. I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change." Sheeran also rejected the suggestion that his decision not to speak publicly about his personal beliefs made him indifferent to the conflict. "I am not complicit," he wrote. "I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care." MICK JAGGER DOESN'T WANT TO 'LECTURE' FANS, SAYS HIS JOB IS TO MAKE PEOPLE 'HAVE THE BEST TIME' However, his statement has done little to quiet the criticism. "Wicked" actor Marissa Bode accused Sheeran of lacking a backbone, writing that although she uses a wheelchair, she still has a "f---ing spine," before adding her support for Palestine on Instagram. "Ed Sheeran, my legs may not work like they used to before, but at least I have a f---ing spine. Free Palestine, b----," she wrote. Children’s educator and YouTube sensation Ms. Rachel similarly said Sheeran had "caved" to people who opposed Macklemore’s advocacy and argued that silence over Gaza is not neutral. "Ed Sheeran had an opportunity [to] show that we won’t be bullied into punishing people for supporting Palestine. Instead he caved to people who refuse to accept what the world knows. A genocide is happening in Gaza. We all need to speak out against it." "I just have a little message for you," he said in a video he shared on social media. "There are two kinds of people in this world, Ed. There are people who do the right thing. That rapper Macklemore would be one of those people. And there are people, many of them sadly little – excuse me, I nearly used the F-word then, p----s like you who do the wrong thing. Goodbye." Macklemore has also criticized Sheeran’s stance, though he said their friendship was not necessarily over. Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Irish folk band Beoga all announced that they would withdraw from upcoming dates in solidarity with Macklemore. Finneas said artists should not be silenced when speaking for oppressed people, while Rowe condemned the use of wealth and venue power to suppress pro-Palestinian voices. Lukas Graham wrote that he was grateful for his friendship with Sheeran, but couldn't "carry on with tour as things stand," before withdrawing. "I'm sorry we won't be there. This is a difficult decision, but it's one I need to stand by," Graham added. A week after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" while opening for Sheeran, the rapper was dropped from the remaining U.S. dates he was scheduled to perform on the "Shape of You" singer's tour. "As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans," Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s "Loop Tour," said in a statement to Rolling Stone. articles.title: Leno says he gets 'beat up' rhetorically for refusing to go political but refuses to alienate Trump audiences
articles.summary: Jay Leno says he still faces backlash for making fun of both political sides equally, recalling how he and Johnny Carson split jokes across party lines.
articles.body: Jay Leno said in an interview released Sept. 9 that he continues to face criticism for avoiding partisan comedy, telling the "Unexpired" podcast that performing for politically mixed audiences — including Trump supporters in states like Indianameans his priority remains getting laughs rather than delivering political commentary. Leno, who hosted NBC’s "The Tonight Show" for more than two decades, explained why he believes comedians working outside the late-night television environment have to account for audiences with a range of political views. "I get beat up for this all the time, but as someone who works in the real world, when you go to Indiana, I'm sorry, a third of your audience is going to be Trump people," Leno said. CRAIG FERGUSON REVEALS WHY TRUMP JOKES ARE MISSING FROM HIS NEW COMEDY TOUR Christian Toto, an entertainment journalist, film critic and founder of Hollywood in Toto, told Fox News Digital Wednesday that Leno's approach reflects what he sees as a divide between touring stand-ups and television hosts who have cultivated more politically defined audiences. Toto founded Hollywood in Toto in 2014 and covers entertainment and culture. "Late-night hosts don't care who they alienate in 2026. They've chosen an audience. Period. Jimmy Kimmel infamously said of his Republican fans, ‘not good riddance,' but riddance. That says it all," Toto said. Leno told host Kim Alexis that his objective onstage remains entertainment, recalling that he and former "Tonight Show" host Johnny Carson deliberately tried to spread political jokes across party lines rather than consistently targeting one side. "I mean, Johnny and I used to pride ourselves on making fun of both sides equally. Now I get beaten up for that. But OK, that's all right," Leno said. CONAN O'BRIEN, ZACH GALIFIANAKIS SAY IT'S A 'MISCONCEPTION' THAT COMEDY SHOWS ONLY TARGET CONSERVATIVES Leno has made similar comments repeatedly in recent years. A few years ago, he said he had stopped putting politics in his stand-up because audiences increasingly wanted to know whether a joke was "for or against" their side before hearing the punchline. In a 2025 interview at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library, Leno again said he believed political humor worked best when audiences could laugh when their own side became the target. Kimmel has publicly acknowledged losing some Republican viewers as his show became more politically outspoken. During a 2017 "CBS Sunday Morning" interview, Kimmel was asked whether he minded Republican viewers abandoning the program after his commentary on his healthcare and gun policy. "Well, not good riddance, but riddance," Kimmel said. JIMMY KIMMEL SAYS HE FELT 'DEFEATED' AFTER COLBERT SHOW WAS CANCELED, SAYS CBS IS USING 'MADE-UP NUMBERS' Toto also pointed to Jimmy Fallon’s 2016 interview with then-presidential candidate Donald Trump, when the "Tonight Show" host tousled Trump’s hair. Fallon later said he regretted not responding more directly to the criticism that followed and denied that the lighthearted segment was intended to "normalize" Trump. "Jimmy Fallon had a chance to be the new Jay Leno, the apolitical yukster who just wanted to make the country laugh," Toto said. "Sadly, after he tousled Donald Trump's hair on ‘The Tonight Show’ in 2016, he was hounded by the media and the left for humanizing the real estate mogul." Leno returned to the subject this summer, telling Deadline that modern audiences are "all over the place" politically while discussing changes to late-night television. He also called Joe Rogan "the new Johnny Carson," pointing to podcasts as an increasingly important alternative to traditional late-night shows. articles.title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million, 21,000-sq-ft Ohio mansion privacy fence plans hit hurdle; Bratenahl board delays approval; neighbours raise concerns over Lake Erie views and property values
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s plans to fence off their new $5.35 million lakeside mansion in Ohio have run into a hurdle, with the village’s archite.
articles.body: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s plans to fence off their new $5.35 million lakeside mansion in Ohio have run into a hurdle, with the village’s architectural review board considering the proposal twice but failing to approve it, according to the Daily Mail.The couple is seeking greater privacy at their new Lake Erie estate by installing a higher fence around the property. They have also reportedly installed a voice warning system after concerns over people getting too close to the home.Fence proposal faces Bratenahl rulesThe fence proposal first appeared on the agenda of the Bratenahl Architectural Review Board on August 11, a day after the agenda had already been published. It resurfaced on September 8 under old business, indicating that the board had previously reviewed the plans without reaching a decision.Bratenahl’s zoning rules could prove challenging for the couple. Fences along the lakefront are generally limited to 2.5 feet in height unless at least 75% of the fence is see-through.The regulations state that the restriction is intended to protect “the shoreline, views of Lake Erie and property values.”Kelce purchased the property through an LLC in March and initially sought an 8-foot fence around the estate, which would not comply with the village code. Following discussions with village officials and neighbors, the couple agreed to reduce the proposed height and decided that a fence around the entire property was unnecessary.A village official confirmed to the publication that a new permit application for the fence has been submitted.Couple installs warning system at mansionWhile the fence proposal remains unresolved, Swift and Kelce have taken another step to increase security around their new home.Page Six reported that the couple recently installed a voice warning system around the property. A nearby resident told the publication that a neighbor who approached the house received an automated warning after getting too close to the property.Kelce will also have to return before the village board for approval of landscaping work planned for the property in October, although an exact meeting date has not yet been set, according to records.Village officials reportedly described the applicant as “gracious” while working with the municipality.Neighbors could object to fence plansBefore the village building commissioner can issue a permit for construction work, the architectural review board must approve the design. Under village rules, objections from neighboring property owners can also affect the approval process.Swift and Kelce’s 3.5-acre estate directly borders two properties, with the neighboring homes sharing more than 600 feet of boundary with the property. Three additional households across the road are also entitled to object under the village code.The couple’s immediate neighbors have previously raised objections over fencing at the same property.Neighbors previously opposed pool fenceIn 2023, the two neighboring households filed written objections to a pool fence at the address that is now owned by Swift and Kelce. Both residents subsequently appeared before the same architectural review board to argue against the proposal.Eric Stephenson, who purchased the house northeast of the property for $782,000 in 2018, brought photographs taken from his dining room to demonstrate how he believed the fence could affect his view.“Part of the beauty of living in there is that it's open space where you can look and we're all one yard,” he told the board at the time.He also argued that preserving sightlines to Lake Erie was important to the character and value of the surrounding properties.On the other side of the estate, Katherine Bolton, who has owned her home with her husband Bill since 1990, also spoke against the proposed fence.“One of the wonderful things about Bratenahl are the open vistas and the view lines,” she said, arguing that open space should be preserved to maintain the village’s historic character.Bill Bolton is a former president of the Bratenahl village council.2023 fence dispute was differentThe 2023 dispute involved a different type of fence. At the time, the village required a safety barrier around a newly constructed pool, while the property owner did not want the fence.The architectural review board ultimately approved the pool fence by a 2-1 vote despite the neighbors’ objections.The circumstances are different this time. In 2023, the property owner and the neighbors opposed the fence, whereas Swift and Kelce are now seeking one while their neighbors have previously expressed concerns about fencing at the property.Inside Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s Ohio mansionThe property was previously owned by a Middleburg Heights construction company, which purchased the mansion for $1.95 million in March 2023.After restoring the gatehouse and adding a heated pool and bluestone patio, the property was sold to Kelce for $5.35 million in March.The house was purchased solely by Kelce through an LLC created specifically for the property. The company was incorporated in Ohio on February 26 and was used to purchase the estate seven days later.The 21,000-square-foot mansion features eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms and a two-bedroom guest cottage. Built in 1895, the property also includes a ballroom that has been converted into a game room and home theatre.The village has not yet published minutes from either the August or September meetings, leaving the precise details of the latest fence application unclear.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Happily married Florida mom charged after arrest exposes alleged love triangle involving her son
articles.summary: A domestic violence call in Polk County, Florida, unraveled a secret love triangle after Shane Clemens told deputies he'd been sleeping with his mother.
articles.body: Police in Polk County, Florida had no idea what they were walking into when they were called out to the Clemens' residence for a domestic dispute between a mother and her son. There was much more going on than allegations that Shane Clemens, 22, had battered his mother, Christina Clemens, 46, during a reported domestic violence incident. articles.title: Resident Evil is a comedy first and a thrilling nightmare second
articles.summary: Zach Cregger’s new Resident Evil film — in theaters September — highlights how video game movies have evolved.
articles.body: When Paul W.S. Anderson’s Resident Evil hit theaters in 2002, video game movies were largely seen as a niche. Films like Mortal Kombat and Tomb Raider had proven that big-screen game adaptations could be successful, but the commercial and critical failure of projects like the 1993 Super Mario Bros. still cast a long shadow. And while Anderson’s vision of Raccoon City might have captivated audiences on the whole, many hardcore fans of Capcom’s games were left disappointed by the way the original movies wildly deviated from the source material. Weapons director Zach Cregger’s new take on Resident Evil is a return to the franchise’s fundamentals and a choice example of how video game movies have evolved. Its story is stripped down and its zombified monsters are terrifying. It’s also chiefly a movie that’s trying to make you laugh. Cregger uses humor to amplify his Resident Evil’s horror — his spin on the games’ infected ghouls are meant to be as funny as they are disturbing. The film feels like it could be the beginning of a fantastic new era for the franchise, but what’s most impressive is how well it can work as one and done. Though this Resident Evil is peppered with nods to Capcom’s games, it focuses on Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier character created for the movie. Like most people living in his mountain town, Bryan knows that a drive over to Raccoon City in the middle of winter can be hell, but a last-minute, high-paying delivery gig is enough to convince him to make the trip. Even with the treacherous weather and spotty cellphone reception, Bryan’s journey with his mysterious cargo is mostly uneventful as he first sets out. But he begins to understand what kind of danger he’s wandering into when he accidentally runs over a shambling woman (Andrea Miltnerová) who doesn’t seem to realize that she’s just been hit by an out-of-control car. [Media: Resident Evil’s first big scare almost immediately establishes the sense of humor Cregger leans into throughout the film. You can feel the fear oozing out of Bryan as he trudges into the woods looking for the woman, but that tension momentarily evaporates as the film smash-cuts to him coaxing her into his car so that he can get her the medical help she clearly needs. The same dread rushes to the fore when Bryan witnesses how Resident Evil’s infected humans can mutate into creatures that feel like nods to Katamari Damacy and The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. But it’s hard not to laugh when Bryan muses about how interesting the zombies’ transformations are to see up close. Cregger knows that while viewers might not be familiar with Resident Evil’s lore, we can all appreciate how horror movies need their characters to make poor decisions. Abrams plays Bryan with a wide-eyed guilelessness that’s charming, but what really makes the character work is the way each monster encounter forces him to evolve into someone with better survival instincts. By building the film around a civilian instead of highly trained special agents, Cregger and co-writer Shay Hatten give themselves the ability to tell a story that leans into the survival aspect of survival horror. Because Bryan is a bit of a dolt who’s constantly screaming in terror and fumbling his bullets when he’s scared, it often feels like the movie is replicating the experience of playing (or watching someone else play) a Resident Evil game for the first time. Bryan finds a couple of guns and a very limited number of bullets, but they’re nowhere near enough to make him feel safe as he trudges toward Raccoon City making the occasional stop to search seemingly empty buildings in hopes of finding a way to call for help. The movie’s indoor scenes where Bryan’s rifling through drawers and tiptoeing down dark hallways are its most suspenseful because Cregger establishes early on that danger is always lurking just around the corner. Those moments are when it really seems like Cregger is channeling the essence of Capcom’s games, but you can also feel the director winking at his audience whenever Bryan talks about video games teaching him how to navigate his situation. [Image: There’s a general straightforwardness to Cregger’s Resident Evil that sets it apart from many other recent video game adaptations. The film isn’t as concerned with overall character development as The Last of Us and its set pieces aren’t as large as The Super Mario Galaxy Movie’s. But those qualities work in the movie’s favor because they help draw your attention to all of the imaginative ways Cregger interpolates classic elements of Resident Evil storytelling and gameplay. Especially coming after Weapons, Resident Evil feels like Cregger putting his mark on a beloved gaming property while breathing new life into a film franchise that was always fun, but lost its way as it grew in scale. Cregger has found a way to make the world of Resident Evil seem primed for more cinematic exploration, and to show us how far video game movies have come. Resident Evil also stars Zach Cherry, Will Merrick, Zoé Bellas, Chris Lew Kum Hoi, Griffin Newman, and Magdalena Sittovaas. The movie hits theaters on September 18th.

articles.title: The 2.5-hour AI-generated Odyssey movie is 2.5 hours too long
articles.summary: The Odyssey dominated theaters, and a new AI version is hoping to build off of that energy.
articles.body: Christopher Nolan’s engrossing take on The Odyssey dominated at the box office and spurred a newfound interest in classic literature among filmgoers. But a new retelling of the story made entirely with AI is so bad that it might just make viewers hate the original tale altogether. The new film, called Odysseus: The Fall, comes via AI firm Fountain 0 and is written and directed by company cofounder Ash Koosha, who also lent his likeness to the title character and created all of the music. (The film’s credits are very short.) The studio’s only previous work is an AI film called Dreams of Violets that made it into Tribeca earlier this year. The Fall is, on its face, a much more ambitious project, billed as “the first completely AI generated film produced at the level of a Hollywood blockbuster.” In reality, it’s nothing close to “the level of a Hollywood blockbuster.” That may not necessarily be surprising, but after watching the entire 2.5-hour production I nonetheless found myself constantly surprised by just how much worse things could get. The Fall is the opposite of a glimpse at the future of AI filmmaking — it’ll make you wonder if there’s really any future in it at all. The movie is available to rent now for $9.99 and, as far as I can tell, you can only watch it via a web browser. In order to view it on my living room TV I had to mirror the screen from my phone, which is not exactly IMAX in 70mm. Things didn’t get much better once I pressed play. The Fall is plagued by two main issues. The first is consistency. The world of the film is constantly morphing, to the point that it’s incredibly distracting. The height of the cyclops that traps Odysseus and his men changes from shot to shot, waves move in the opposite direction of the wind, mouths don’t match the words spoken (and sometimes they move without producing a sound at all), and oars bend and twist as sailors row. In one scene a huge fleet of boats is racing through the ocean and one of them is inexplicably moving sideways. The AI-produced voice-overs can be incomprehensible, and at various points the names of both Odysseus and Zeus are pronounced wrong. If it were just the odd hiccup it might be understandable, but there are so many faults in The Fall that it can be hard to focus on anything else. I watched the movie with my 13-year-old kid and it basically became a game of finding the weirdest mistakes. I noticed that a sword magically turned into a dagger, and then she one-upped me by spotting an alien carcass roasting over a spit. The Fall seems like a film designed to prove why script supervisors exist. [Media: The thing is, while all of the AI-induced errors are distracting, they’re also the most entertaining part of the movie. There isn’t really much to distract from in The Fall because it is so dull. Because current AI models are really only capable of generating scenes that last a few seconds, the movie feels like a disjointed collection of moments from the odyssey that have been stitched together with little rhyme or reason. If you didn’t already know the story going into this, I don’t think you’d have any idea of what was going on, because the film explains very little. You don’t even learn about Penelope’s suitors until the movie is almost over. I also can’t think of a single aspect of The Fall that feels improved because of AI. The “acting” is bafflingly bad, with characters pausing for seconds at a time for no apparent reason and bursts of laughter that jolt you out of nowhere. There’s no weight to the action, as if this takes place in a world where things like physics and gravity are suggestions rather than constants. Similarly, there aren’t any cool or impressive effects that wouldn’t be possible without the technology. The monsters look like shabby stop-motion creatures from the 1930s, which is all the weirder when they’re put beside the smooth, hyperreal human characters that AI spews out. It’s not just jarring, it’s boring and ugly. Koosha claims that he adapted this story because he “always felt passionately about Homer’s epic tale since [he] originally read it years ago.” It seems much more likely that he’s trying to skate by on the hype and energy created by Nolan’s film, turning AI slop into a modern-day iteration of direct-to-video cash grabs. But this also puts the film at an incredible disadvantage from the very beginning, inviting comparisons to one of the most critically and commercially successful movies of the last few years, one that was especially beloved because of the director’s insistence on human craftsmanship. Nolan is someone who cares deeply about film, and his passion and enthusiasm is why stars want to work with him and viewers flock the theaters to see his movies. The existence of The Fall, meanwhile, shows utter contempt for the medium, attempting to boil the work of hundreds of skilled workers into slop produced by a tiny team. It’s so terrible it’ll make you appreciate human-made art all the more.

articles.body:
Náutico and Operário-PR drew 3-3 in the 28th round of Série B Credits: Rafael Vieira/CNC

Four goals in the final 15 minutes of Náutico vs. Operário-PR set the score at 3-3 at the Aflitos in Recife on Tuesday night (15). After Vinicius put the home side ahead with 56 seconds on the clock, Vinícius Diniz leveled it near the end of the first half.

Until the 37th minute of the second half, the score was 1-1, when Jean Carlos scored for Timbu from the penalty spot. Danielzinho added to the lead in the 42nd minute. With a 3-1 advantage on the scoreboard, victory looked like the natural outcome for Náutico.

Fantasma, in a surprising comeback, pulled one back with a stunning free-kick goal by Boschilia in the 48th minute and equalized through Cuenú two minutes later.

The result left Operário-PR in eighth place with 44 points, six more than Náutico, who sit 14th.

In addition to the eventful draw, the night also featured Londrina-PR's 6-0 thrashing of Ponte Preta at Vitorino Gonçalves Dias in Londrina. Hebert (2), João Vitor, Vitinho , Igor Bahia, and Guilherme Portuga found the net. The Paraná side is trying to climb out of the relegation zone. They have 28 points and are three behind 16th-placed Botafogo-SP. Ponte remains bottom of the table with ten.

In a Northeastern clash, CRB beat Sport 2-1 at Rei Pelé in Maceió with goals from Crystopher and Hereda, moving into seventh place with 47 points. Patrick de Paula pulled one back for Leão da Ilha do Retiro, who are ninth with 41.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran: veja quem foi contra e quem defendeu expulsão de rapper da turnê | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão de afastar rapper Macklemore gerou reação em cadeia de músicos convidados, deixando turnê sem atrações de abertura e sem banda que o acompanhava em parte do show.
articles.summary: Decisão de afastar rapper Macklemore gerou reação em cadeia de músicos convidados, deixando turnê sem atrações de abertura e sem banda que o acompanhava em parte do show.
articles.body:
Após uma declaração pró-Palestina do rapper Macklemore, o cantor Ed Sheeran se viu no centro de uma grande polêmica. Isso porque o rapper era um dos artistas de abertura da sua turnê e acabou sendo retirado das apresentações seguintes pela produção dos espetáculos.

A decisão acabou gerando uma série de comentários, alguns defendendo a decisão e a atitude de Ed Sheeran e equipe, outros presetando apoio a Macklemore e sua saída.

O próprio cantor divulgou um longo comunicado na segunda-feira (14) sobre sua saída da turnê.

"Antes de começar, quero dizer algo que deveria ser óbvio. Neste momento, acho que isso importa. Eu não sou uma vítima", escreveu Macklemore no Instagram.

"Temos carreiras, dinheiro, oportunidades, segurança e público no mundo todo. Quaisquer que sejam as consequências que enfrentemos pelo que dizemos, podemos voltar para casa e para nossas famílias. As vítimas são os palestinos."

Já Ed Sheeran afirmou que a decisão partiu da promotora da turnê, a Messina Touring Group.

"Não sou cúmplice. Tenho minhas visões pessoais sobre esse conflito devastador. Só porque eu escolho não falar publicamente, não significa que eu não as tenho, e não significa que eu não me importe", publicou Sheeran.

Os cantores Finneas, Aaron Rowe e Lukas Graham e a banda Beoga declararam nesta terça-feira (15) que não vão mais abrir os shows de Ed Sheeran.

Com isso, Sheeran perdeu todos os artistas de abertura de sua série de concertos, que tem datas previstas até 11 de dezembro.

Finneas, aliás, abriria as apresentações do cantor britânico em São Paulo nos dias 5 e 6 de dezembro. O grupo Beoga, além de abrir shows, também se apresentava ao lado de Sheeran em trechos de repertório influenciados pela música tradicional irlandesa.

Junto à decisão de cancelamento, os três cantores e o grupo manifestaram apoio à causa palestina.

"Artistas não devem ser silenciados por se manifestar contra a opressão", escreveu Finneas no Instagram.

"Deveríamos poder falar sobre guerra, sobre civis sendo mortos, sobre crianças que merecem crescer. Onde quer que vivam. Qualquer que seja a sua bandeira", afirmou Graham.

"Como irlandeses, conhecemos bem até demais genocídio, fome forçada e ocupação violenta", disse Rowe.

"Somos irlandeses que entendem colonialismo. Como membros fundadores do movimento Artistas Irlandeses pela Palestina, somos ativistas com compromisso pela justiça e continuaremos a ser", publicou a banda Beoga.

Sheeran ainda não comentou a saída dos demais artistas da turnê.

Ed Sheeran se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2024 — Foto: Leo Franco/AgNews

O ator Javier Bardem usou sua conta no Instagram para convocar abertamente um boicote a Ed Sheeran.

O espanhou criticou a justificativa de Ed Sheeran e da produtora de manter a turnê como um ambiente estritamente neutro e despolitizado.

O cantor Ed Sheeran se viu no centro de uma polêmica em torno de sua turnê "Loop" após um discurso pró-Palestina do rapper Macklemore.

Também pelo Instagram, a cantora Pink repostou uma mensagem que criticava o rapper e sua manifestação.

Após a repercussão negativa da primeira postagem, a cantora publicou um longo texto.

"Nunca pedi que outro artista fosse silenciado e não estou pedindo agora. Não preciso que ninguém seja demitido, e não preciso de reembolso. O que eu preciso é poder dizer, como mãe judia, que aquilo me assustou, e assustou pessoas que amo."

Já Robert Kraft, dono de um dos estádios com show de Ed Sheeran marcado, defendeu a decisão ressaltando o caráter apolítico e unificador do artista, além de assumir publicamente para si e para os estádios a responsabilidade pelo veto.

"Esta decisão é resultado de seus comentários [Macklemore] e de um histórico mais amplo de retórica e imagens antissemitas que consideramos profundamente ofensivas e prejudiciais à comunidade judaica."

Tudo começou no dia 4 de setembro. Segundo o jornal "The Guardian", o rapper americano, que fazia o show de abertura no MetLife Stadium, em Nova Jersey (EUA), gritou "Free Palestine" (Palestina Livre, em tradução literal) . Ele também afirmou que queria que as pessoas em Gaza e na Cisjordânia soubessem que não haviam sido esquecidas.

A declaração motivou uma petição do Conselho Israelense-Americano (Israeli American Council) pedindo a exclusão do rapper da turnê.

A Messina Touring Group, promotora responsável pela etapa dos Estados Unidos da turnê de Sheeran, informou à revista "Rolling Stone" que Macklemore não faria os shows das datas restantes .

"Como promotora da turnê 'Loop' de Ed Sheeran nos Estados Unidos, fomos informados pelos locais que sediarão as próximas datas da turnê de que eles não permitirão a realização dos shows com Macklemore no line-up. Isso resultaria no cancelamento da turnê e impactaria centenas de milhares de fãs. Após discussões com as partes envolvidas, Macklemore não se apresentará nas datas restantes como atração de apoio."

O rapper estava escalado para abrir oito dos dez shows restantes da turnê pelos EUA , com retomada prevista para 19 de setembro na Filadélfia. As cidades com locais de apresentação que teriam se oposto ao retorno de Macklemore incluem Boston, Atlanta, Charlotte, Indianápolis, Dallas e Tampa.

Um comitê de investigação contratado pela Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) apontou em junho que Israel alvejou crianças deliberadamente na Faixa de Gaza. Segundo a comissão, tais práticas em Gaza configuram genocídio, crimes contra a humanidade e crimes de guerra.

O relatório da comissão da ONU afirmou ainda que cerca de 30% dos 73 mil mortos na guerra em Gaza eram crianças, pouco mais de 20 mil em números absolutos.

articles.title: XV Festival de Gastronomia de Macaé consolida sucesso e aquece economia local | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento reuniu multidão na Orla dos Cavaleiros com pratos exclusivos, aulas-show com chefs renomados, atrações culturais e tecnologia.
articles.summary: Evento reuniu multidão na Orla dos Cavaleiros com pratos exclusivos, aulas-show com chefs renomados, atrações culturais e tecnologia.
articles.body:
Milhares de moradores e visitantes passaram pela orla durante a 15ª edição do festival — Foto: Arquivo Secom

O XV Festival de Cultura e Gastronomia de Macaé marcou a Orla dos Cavaleiros ao movimentar o público e fortalecer o setor produtivo do município durante cinco dias de programação. Ao todo, 23 estabelecimentos participantes apresentaram menus exclusivos de entradas, pratos principais e sobremesas. O evento impulsionou o turismo, gerou postos de trabalho e ampliou o movimento em hotéis, pousadas, comércio e prestadores de serviços da cidade.

Sob o tema “Terroir”, a edição colocou em evidência os ingredientes nativos e a identidade culinária da região. Esse conceito também guiou o espaço "Cozinha Show", onde mais de 20 especialistas e chefs de destaque nacional e internacional — como Frédéric Monnier, Bruno Katz, Vanessa Rocha, Cristiana Beltrão e Pedro Coronha — ministraram oficinas gratuitas sobre café, vinhos, coquetelaria, pescados e valorização da gastronomia local.

Estrutura trouxe novidades como o espaço Boulevard e área de regulação sensorial — Foto: Arquivo Secom

A estrutura à beira-mar ofereceu atrações para toda a família, unindo apresentações de música e dança, área infantil e iniciativas voltadas à inclusão. Entre os diferenciais da edição estiveram o Espaço de Regulação Sensorial, voltado para o acolhimento de pessoas com sensibilidade a ruídos; a Sala de Notebook com Wi-Fi gratuito; e as interações com o robô humanoide "Fred", que fez sucesso entre adultos e crianças.

Outro marco foi o espaço "Boulevard", ambiente dedicado a aproximar os frequentadores de produtores regionais, além de reunir vinícolas, bares de drinks e cervejarias artesanais. O envolvimento dos restaurantes e a grande adesão do público confirmam a relevância da iniciativa para o calendário cultural, turístico e econômico de Macaé.

articles.title: Macklemore donates $1M to Palestinian aid organizations after Ed Sheeran tour fallout
articles.summary: Macklemore is donating $1 million from Ed Sheeran's U.S. "Loop Tour" to Palestinian aid groups and challenged Robert Kraft to match his contribution.
articles.body: Macklemore announced that he is donating the $1 million he earned opening for Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour to organizations providing humanitarian aid to Palestinians, prompting a public response from New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft. On Monday, the 43-year-old rapper was dropped from Sheeran's "Loop Tour" after he repeatedly called for a "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" during his opening act at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey on Sept. 4 and 5. Macklemore alleged that Kraft, 85, pressured Sheeran to remove him from the tour by telling the singer he would not be allowed to perform at Gillette Stadium and by rallying other stadium owners to issue a similar ultimatum. Kraft later confirmed he opposed Macklemore's participation at Gillette based on what he described as the "Thrift Shop" rapper's history of antisemitic rhetoric. ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO Sheeran, 35, has said the decision was made by the tour promoter and venue owners, not by him personally. In an Instagram post on Wednesday, Macklemore shared his plans to donate his paycheck from the "Loop Tour" to six organizations including the Palestine Children's Relief Fund (PCRF), HEAL Palestine, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians, UNRWA USA National Committee and American Near East Refugee Aid (ANERA). "With everything that has happened over the last 48 hours, I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation, and still fighting for their freedom," he wrote. "I will be donating the entire $1 million of my net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour to six organizations working directly to support the Palestinian people," he continued. "And I invite Robert Kraft to match my donation. Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protecting. A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any other life on this earth." "I want to center the parents carrying their children into hospitals without the basic resources to treat them, and the physicians, paramedics, journalists and aid workers who keep going back in. I want to center the organizers and activists who have paid real costs for standing with Palestine," Macklemore added. "Their risk is of a far different order than mine." HANNAH EINBINDER'S BRUTAL MESSAGE TO ED SHEERAN FUELS GROWING CELEBRITY REVOLT OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR DRAMA Macklemore noted that "writing a check is one of the least costly forms of solidarity to me." "I am doing it because I can and because these organizations are doing the work while much of the world debates it," he wrote. "Palestinians have lived for decades without basic rights and should not have to wait another day to be free," Macklemore added. "That is where my focus will remain. I will continue to stand with the Palestinian people and their fight for liberation." MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE "When the news cycle moves on, which it will, don’t move with it," he concluded. "Free Palestine." Shortly after the rapper challenged Kraft to match his contribution, Kraft said Sheeran had already asked him to commit $2 million to match the singer's own donation toward humanitarian relief in the region. Earlier today, before Macklemore challenged me to match his donation, Ed called me and asked me to commit $2 million to match his donation to aid in the region and fight this humanitarian crisis," Kraft wrote in a statement shared on Gillette Stadium's social media pages. MACKLEMORE'S LONG HISTORY OF CONTROVERSY FROM GRAMMY WINS TO 'FREE PALESTINE' CONCERT REMARKS "Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges," Kraft continued. articles.title: The streamers are fighting over Halloween
articles.summary: At TIFF 2026, the likes of Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, AMC Plus, and Peacock all showed off new horror series coming in October.
articles.body: The Toronto International Film Festival is a place to go to see the future of film, but this year it also provided a glimpse at what is coming very soon in the realm of streaming. Four different streamers — Peacock, Netflix, Amazon, and AMC — all premiered early looks at upcoming horror-adjacent series that are dropping very soon. And by doing it at TIFF, they showed just how important the month of October has become in the realm of streaming. Perhaps the most high-profile is Carrie, which is coming to Prime Video. An adaptation of the classic Stephen King novel, which has already been turned into no fewer than three feature films, this version of Carrie is notable in particular because of who is helming it. Mike Flanagan has done a handful of King adaptations in the past — including Doctor Sleep and The Life of Chuck — but the director is perhaps best-known for his work on limited series for Netflix. That includes the likes of The Haunting of Hill House, Midnight Mass, and The Fall of the House of Usher. Those series came out on a near-annual basis between 2018 and 2023, making Flanagan’s particular blend of dramatic horror a staple of Netflix in October. [Media: Then, in 2022, Amazon poached Flanagan to work on projects for Prime Video. The first of these is Carrie, which starts streaming on October 7th. It still tells largely the same story as its predecessors — a young girl’s destructive psychic powers awaken after getting bullied in high school — but it updates it in a few ways. For starters, the story has been thoroughly modernized, with much of the bullying happening in cyberspace. But since it’s a series instead of a movie, Carrie also stretches out the story, which gives it the space to explore the teen drama a little, and also adds plenty of opportunities for Flanagan’s trademark lengthy monologues. I’ve only seen the premiere episode so far, but early on it’s a combination of flavors that work really well together. [Media: Netflix, meanwhile, has filled in the gap with a new series called Below, which premieres on October 8th, just a day after Carrie starts streaming. I saw the first two episodes earlier this week — there will be six in total — and while it’s a different kind of story compared to the likes of Hill House, it has a similarly dark and mysterious energy. Below is about what seems to be an ancient sea creature that begins terrorizing a small fishing village in Newfoundland, on the east coast of Canada. From what I’ve seen, the show does a great job of steadily building the terror of the creature’s reveal, while also mixing the scares with a healthy dose of family drama, led by Josh Hartnett as a struggling fisher who is struggling to keep his family together. [Media: Then there’s Peacock, which is joining the fray with a prequel series. Fans of Friday the 13th will know that Jason’s mom plays a pivotal role in the very first film, and the new show Crystal Lake explores how she got to that point. It stars Linda Cardellini as Pamela Voorhees, a single mother who is thrown into a pit of despair and disbelief when her young son drowns to death. I went into the show thinking that I didn’t really need to know much more about the backstory of Jason’s mother, but the first two episodes that premiered at TIFF — and Cardellini’s performance in particular — have me second-guessing that. Crystal Lake is surprisingly tense and dramatic, but, given its connection to Friday the 13th, it also has slasher-movie levels of gore and gross-out deaths, ones that are so brutal they approach comedy. If nothing else, it gets off to a very strong start. All episodes of Crystal Lake hit Peacock on October 15th. Rounding out the list is Yaga, a supernatural detective series that’s coming to AMC Plus on October 23rd. Unfortunately I wasn’t able to catch the premiere screening for the show, but it does seem promising, with a cast that includes Carrie-Anne Moss and Heated Rivalry’s Hudson Williams, and a very intriguing trailer: [Media: What has become abundantly clear in 2026 is that horror is big business. The likes of Backrooms and Obsession have exploded at the box office, while Widow’s Bay had a dominating night at the Emmys. So it only makes sense that streamers are continuing to capitalize on the trend, and using TIFF as a showcase event. October is going to be a very busy month for horror fans.

articles.title: Here’s who’ll be on ‘SNL’ when Season 52 starts next week
articles.summary: Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter will join “Saturday Night Live,” the show announced, while Chloe Fineman previously said she was leaving.
articles.body: “Saturday Night Live” added two new names to its cast for its 52nd season, while another cast member is moving on. Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter will join the sketch comedy show as featured players when it resumes next weekend, “SNL” announced Wednesday. “Welcome to the cast!” the show said on Instagram, in all capital letters. Saidah Belo-Osagie Belo-Osagie is a New Yorker from Queens. She wrote and directed “Tinge,” a short film; created an event series, “Afrobeats Futura”; and had a solo show, “Saidah Gets Closure,” “SNL” said in a news release about the two additions. She shared the “SNL” post on her Instagram Story, writing, “A DREAM COME TRUE.” Grace Reiter Reiter, who is from Chippewa Falls, Wisconsin, co-wrote, directed and stars in the upcoming Netflix show “Minimum Wage,” a series about teenagers running a pizzeria. It’s based on the series released online in 2024, which made waves on TikTok and elsewhere, Netflix said. ‘SNL’ departures Chloe Fineman, who joined the show in 2019 for the 45th season and beyond, said July 16 that she was leaving to try something new. “It’s really hard to leave SNL but it does feel like the right time,” she wrote on Instagram at the time. Fineman spent seven seasons as an “SNL” cast member, performing impressions of Drew Barrymore and Britney Spears and appearing in sketches and advertising spoofs, such as “Domingo,” “Snackhomiez” and “Forever 31.” Deadline reported that Fineman would be joining the cast of “Myron Bolitar,” a Netflix drama series based on Harlan Coben’s thriller novels about a former basketball star who reinvents himself as a sports agent. The annual turnover of cast members can be minimal, indicating that the show and its longtime executive producer, Lorne Michaels, are fine-tuning its cold open, sketches and news segment. Every several years, a greater number of on-air and writers room departures foreshadow a virtual reset for “SNL.” Amid and after the 50th season and its accompanying anniversary specials, the show had some big-name departures, including those of Heidi Gardner, Ego Nwodim and Bowen Yang. Fellow departing talents Michael Longfellow, Devon Walker and Emil Wakim held the freshman-like title “featured player,” a position that often leads to repertory player status. Season 52 of “SNL” premieres Sept. 26 with New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson as host and musical guest Katseye. “SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News.

articles.title: ‘Haiwaan’ box office collection day 6: Saif Ali Khan and Akshay Kumar film continues to slide, collects Rs 55 lakh on Wednesday
articles.summary: ‘Haiwaan’ is struggling to find its footing at the box office. Directed by Priyadarshan, the Saif Ali Khan and Akshay Kumar starrer opened to Rs. 3 cr.
articles.body: ‘Haiwaan’ is struggling to find its footing at the box office. Directed by Priyadarshan, the Saif Ali Khan and Akshay Kumar starrer opened to Rs. 3 crore last Friday, but a lukewarm response from critics and audiences sent its earnings tumbling soon after. The film brought in Rs. 7.35 crore net in India during its opening weekend, only to see collections plunge to a mere Rs. 70 lakh net on Monday, a number that held steady into Tuesday.Haiwaan's day 6 collection in India and overseasAccording to Sacnilk, the film dipped further on day six, Wednesday, earning Rs. 55 lakh and pushing its total to Rs. 9.30 crore net in India. Meanwhile, the film's overseas performance hasn't fared much better. It added Rs. 10 lakh gross internationally, bringing its overseas total to Rs. 3.25 crore gross, while the worldwide gross now stands at Rs. 14.36 crore.Haiwaan's budget versus collectionThe makers of ‘Haiwaan’ haven't officially disclosed the film's budget, but reports suggest it was made for around Rs. 100-115 crore. Weighed against its current earnings, the film is shaping up to be a massive box office disaster.What ‘Haiwaan’ is about‘Haiwaan’ centres on Shyam (Saif Ali Khan), a blind maintenance manager at a building, who becomes the target of Parshuram (Akshay Kumar), a serial killer driven by vengeance. After Parshuram takes revenge by killing Judge Pradhan (Boman Irani), whom he blames for wrongly convicting him, he turns his attention to the judge's daughter, Nandini (Pahal Chaudhary), whose whereabouts only Shyam knows. What follows is a high-stakes clash of strength and strategy, with Shyam risking everything to keep Nandini safe, all while hiding a secret that threatens to turn things upside down. articles.title: Karra Elejalde: "Como La Masía para el Barcelona en el fútbol, el mundo del cortometraje es la cantera del cine"
articles.standfirst: El veterano actor y Kandido Uranga protagonizan 'El triplete', el cortometraje ganador de la VI edición de Audi Future Stories
articles.summary: El veterano actor y Kandido Uranga protagonizan 'El triplete', el cortometraje ganador de la VI edición de Audi Future Stories
articles.body: Hay amistades que sobreviven al paso del tiempo, a las despedidas y hasta a la ausencia. Sobre esa idea, tan sencilla como universal, se construye 'El triplete', el cortometraje ganador de la VI edición de Audi Future Stories, que convierte la amistad, la vejez y la importancia de cumplir una promesa en el punto de partida de una historia tan emotiva como divertida. Rodado recientemente en Barcelona, el filme sigue a Antonio y Mariano, dos residentes de una residencia de ancianos que, tras perder a su inseparable amigo Ezequiel, emprenden una disparatada aventura para evitar que las cenizas de su compañero terminen en un cenicero común. Al frente de esta particular historia de amistad se encuentran dos intérpretes de enorme trayectoria y personalidad: Karra Elejalde y Kandido Uranga. Dos actores que, desde registros diferentes pero con una misma capacidad para dotar de verdad y humanidad a sus personajes, se meten en la piel de estos dos ancianos dispuestos a llevar hasta las últimas consecuencias el vínculo que les une a su amigo desaparecido. En el caso de Karra Elejalde, más de cuatro décadas de carrera y dos Premios Goya avalan una trayectoria marcada por la versatilidad; Kandido Uranga, por su parte, llega al proyecto tras una extensa carrera en cine y televisión y después de haber sido reconocido con el Premio Feroz y nominado al Goya por Maspalomas. 'El triplete' supone además el salto al terreno profesional de Rodrigo Olmedo, ganador de esta edición de Audi Future Stories, una iniciativa que busca impulsar el talento emergente de las escuelas de cine españolas. Para hacer realidad su primer cortometraje profesional, Rodrigo Olmedo ha contado con el acompañamiento del director y productor Kike Maíllo, que ha participado en la codirección y en el desarrollo del proyecto. El resultado es una pieza que combina humor y emoción para hablar del paso del tiempo, de las pérdidas y de esos compromisos que, precisamente porque se adquieren con quienes queremos, adquieren un valor especial. 'El triplete' tendrá su estreno oficial en el marco del Festival Internacional de Cine de San Sebastián. No obstante, antes de que el cortometraje llegue al público, Karra Elejalde y Kandido Uranga han atendido a Tiramillas. PREGUNTA. 'El triplete' habla de la amistad, el paso del tiempo y de cumplir una promesa hasta el final. ¿Qué fue lo que más les conquistó del guion cuando lo leyeron por primera vez? KARRA. Pues es que hay... ¿Cómo diría yo? Hay algo como de rebeldía en dos vejestorios que saben que no son nada y lo dicen. Y que mañana mismo esto se ha acabado. Entonces, ya están en la residencia y se rebelan ante el director. El disgusto es tan grande y la promesa de amistad es tan fuerte que ya hay ciertas edades en las que las personas van y dicen: "Mira, tío, tira para adelante y hagamos lo que nos parece". Y bueno, de eso habla un poco el corto. KANDIDO. Pues precisamente eso, el valor de la amistad y el compromiso que se adquiere con las promesas. PREGUNTA. Antonio y Mariano afrontan la pérdida de un amigo desde el humor, pero también desde una enorme ternura. ¿Cómo se encuentra el equilibrio para interpretar una historia tan emotiva sin caer en el sentimentalismo? KARRA. Pues el equilibrio está en el guion. El actor no se inventa un personaje entero. El guionista ya sabe trasmitir y luego el director te dice hasta qué grado: "Aquí no me llores tanto, aquí llórame un poquito, aquí descojónate...". Entonces ya saben ellos los momentos. Los actores somos los que aparecemos, pero no somos los que decidimos cuánto me voy a emocionar o hasta qué grado me voy a sobrar rozando con la escatología porque estás hablando del gran cariño que le tenias a un amigo y de repente te estás manchado de cenizas suyas. Ahí tienes un poco de humor para contrarrestar el no irnos a algo excesivamente sensiblero. Todo es un arte, pero no corresponde al actor, corresponden al guionista y al director más que al actor. KANDIDO. Leyendo y comprendiendo el guion con atención, siguiendo humilde y respetuosamente las indicaciones de los directores, y finalmente con la complicidad y la verdad de la interpretación entre Karra y yo. PREGUNTA. La película reivindica que la amistad no tiene edad. ¿Creen que el cine ha sabido retratar suficientemente las historias protagonizadas por personas mayores o todavía quedan muchos relatos por contar? KARRA. Hay muy poco, se habla muy poco de la vejez. Siempre, en la historia española, los protagonistas están enfocados en una franja de los 25 a los 50 años, y generalmente gente mucho más joven. Incluso es raro ver una película protagonizada por un señor mayor. Bueno, sí, pero dos de cada cien. Por lo tanto, claro que sí, claro que sí creo que podríamos hacer más películas. Yo rodé 'Auri' con Cristina Marcos, que la dirigía Violeta Salama, y éramos un matrimonio de sexagenarios y éramos los protas. A ver, proporcionalmente se aborda mucho más, lógicamente, el cliente potencial del cine, que está entre los 25 y los 55 años. KANDIDO. No lo sé si suficiente, pero creo que es un buen momento, ya que somos muchas las personas mayores que desde luego tenemos interés por nuestros relatos, que como personas, claro está, son relatos universales. PREGUNTA. La petanca, más allá del deporte, simboliza la unión entre estos tres amigos. ¿Qué representa para ustedes ese triplete que persiguen los protagonistas? KARRA. Pues la petanca son equipos de tres y el tres es el número mágico para un grupo de amigos. Esto lo han dicho siempre, el número tres es la pirámide, es la relación de sociedad. Si hay tres socios en un proyecto, ese proyecto durará más que si hay dos. Pues bueno, es un triplete. Eran tres, uno ha fallecido... Pues a jugar la petanca KANDIDO. Pura Vida. PREGUNTA. Han trabajado con un director consolidado como Kike Maíllo, pero también con Rodrigo Olmedo en su primer cortometraje profesional. ¿Qué les ha sorprendido de su manera de afrontar este proyecto? KARRA. Bueno, a ver, Kike Maíllo es ahí una garantía. Yo creo que la idea es coger a un chico con talento y Kike, bueno, pues saber extraer del director lo que quiere y dejarle hacer, excepto cuando dice: "Mira, por ahí vas mal" o "tío, no tenemos tiempo para esto". Porque Kike ahí hace también un poco de productor, de optimizador, casi de ayudante de dirección: "Oye, coleguita, que hoy tienes todo esto que hacer y si te columpias aquí no llegamos esta tarde". Pero bueno, es una garantía. Kike Maíllo es un veterano y el guion está seleccionado entre casi 300 proyectos por el jurado de Audi Future Stories. Y bueno, Rodrigo Olmedo es algo introvertido, no nos decía muchas cosas a los actores, pero es talentoso y Kike también le dejó su aire. Yo soy más así y entonces se lo facilitaba, le preguntaba: "Oye, tío, ¿y aquí cómo lo ves? ¿Y esto qué tal si lo hago así?". KANDIDO. No sé si sorprender, pero sí destacaría la ilusión, la generosidad, la verdad y la entrega de ambos directores. PREGUNTA. Los dos han defendido públicamente la importancia del cortometraje como puerta de entrada al cine. Mirando atrás, ¿qué papel han tenido los cortos en sus propias carreras y qué consejo darían a quienes empiezan hoy? KARRA. Mira, a quien le guste el fútbol, que a mí no me va demasiado, sabrá que La Fábrica para el Real Madrid y La Masía para el Barcelona son la cantera de la que surgen jugadores para enriquecer al primer equipo, ¿no? Yo he vivido 'Martín' y 'Las seis en punta', dos cortometrajes de Julio Medem. Luego, cuando se consagró como director, rodé con él 'Vacas', 'La ardilla roja' y 'Tierra'. Yo he visto de Juanma Bajo Ulloa dirigir por lo menos cuatro o cinco cortos cuando era un muchacho de 18 o 19 años. Después, como protagonista y ya como gran director, he hecho con él 'Alas de mariposa', 'La madre muerta', 'Airbag' y 'Rey gitano'. Álex de la Iglesia hizo 'Mirindas asesinas' y luego rodé con él 'Acción mutante'. Tuve esa suerte. He tenido la suerte de ver a personas que eran cortometrajistas hace 35 años, ver sus cortos, y luego he tenido la suerte de currar con ellos como directores y ver cómo han progresado todos. Un chico con talento en audiovisuales, el mejor vehículo que tiene para demostrarlo y tener la suerte de que alguien confíe en él es un corto. Para mí, el mundo del cortometraje es la verdadera cantera, porque yo lo he vivido en mis carnes. Estoy dando ejemplos clarísimos de personas cuando eran cortometrajistas, cómo se llamaban sus cortos y cómo luego se convirtieron en grandes directores. Por eso esta oportunidad que da Audi Future Stories a los jóvenes me parece estupenda. KANDIDO. Suma de trabajos y profesionalidad. No me considero quien para dar consejos, pero que luchen por sus quereres. PREGUNTA. Karra, usted ha comentado que un cortometraje permite demostrar el talento para que lleguen nuevas oportunidades. Kandido, usted habla del corto como el futuro de los jóvenes. ¿Creen que iniciativas como Audi Future Stories cubren una necesidad real dentro de la industria? KARRA. Cubren primero una necesidad en la industria del guion. Este guion está seleccionado de entre 300 proyectos. Entonces, una vez tenemos un gran guionista, el siguiente paso es tener a una figura como Kike Maillo que va a garantizar que ese producto va a tener un buen acabado. Y luego confiar en el talento del director y que lo tenga claro. Pero, por supuesto, yo creo que esta iniciativa de Audi y presentar el corto en el Festival de San Sebastián es importante. Quién dice que de estos proyectos no salen el día de mañana grandes directores. KANDIDO. Claro está, es una aportación y hay que felicitar a Audi, pero para cubrir la necesidad real se necesitan muchas más iniciativas de este estilo. PREGUNTA. Ambos acumulan décadas de trayectoria y han trabajado con varias generaciones de cineastas. ¿Qué diferencias encuentran entre los directores jóvenes de hoy y los que conocieron al inicio de sus carreras? KARRA. Las hay, y muchas, entre el digital y el analógico. En el analógico tú tenías 40.000 metros de material para rodar y más te valía tener claro a qué ibas. Ahora, en digital, tú tiras, tiras, tiras y eso sale gratis. Se rodaba a otro ritmo. Ahora haces planos desde distintos ángulos y lo repites 93 veces. Antiguamente decías: "Yo quiero un general de esto". Y luego el corto de este texto, el corto del texto de ella, el corto del texto mío... Se rodaba a otro ritmo. Ahora no, ahora es: "Venga, tira, ya tengo una; venga, vamos a hacer otra". O sea, que la diferencia de cómo se rueda ahora y cómo rodábamos antes es abismal. Pero del mismo modo te diré que también los temas que se abordan y los resultados cinematográficos son distintos, son más actualizados. Eso es indudable. KANDIDO. Sobre todo la diferencia de los tiempos, que incide fundamentalmente en el desarrollo y evolución de la técnica, pero diría que la ilusión y las ganas de hacer cine son bastante parecidas. Hablamos de cine, claro. PREGUNTA. 'El triplete' combina humor y emoción, dos registros que ustedes dominan a la perfección. ¿Es más difícil hacer reír o emocionar cuando una historia habla de temas tan delicados como la pérdida y la despedida? KARRA. Hay que saber tener cintura y saber desenvolverse, o hay que intentarlo. Creo que a mí los retos me interesan y este era uno de ellos. Si estamos hablando de algo tan serio como el fallecimiento de un amigo, muy amigo, que ahora nos falta en nuestro triplete… Y por otra parte estamos haciendo risas, con el hecho de esparcir sus cenizas... KANDIDO. Para contestar a esa pregunta me gustaría oír antes la sensación que la película les provoca a los espectadores. PREGUNTA. El cortometraje se estrenará en el marco del Festival Internacional de Cine de San Sebastián. ¿Qué supone para ustedes presentar un trabajo en un escenario con tanta relevancia para el cine español? KARRA. Supone coger, irte al aeropuerto, ir a Donosti, irte a un hotel, hacer el 'check-in', comprarte un traje o ver uno que no te pones desde hace tres años... Jeje, bueno, estoy bromeando. Yo soy guipuzcoano y Donosti me encanta. Entonces, me gusta ir a presentar un proyecto. También presento la película 'Arriba Tutto' de José Mota. Si no pintas nada en un sitio, no vas. Entonces, en este caso, yo tengo que ir porque tengo dos cositas que presentar y, bueno, pues espero que sean bien recibidas, que gusten. Y allí están mis amigos, así que me tomaré unos calimochos y me lo pasaré de puta madre. KANDIDO. Satisfacción, alegría y gratitud. PREGUNTA. Después de tantos años de profesión, ¿qué proyectos son los que más les siguen ilusionando: los grandes rodajes o historias pequeñas como esta, donde el peso recae en los personajes y las emociones? KARRA. Yo soy un poco perejil de todas las salsas. Me lo paso de puta madre en una superproducción, pero también me lo paso de puta madre haciendo 'Vasil' con Avelina Prat y un actor polaco llamado Ivan Barnev que es una maravilla. Me gusta hacer películas, producciones potentes... Me acuerdo de 'Los últimos de Filipinas', que nos fuimos a Malabo y estábamos allí Javi Gutiérrez, Luis Tosar, Álvaro Cervantes, Ricardo Gómez... Entonces, bueno, hay veces que estás en cosas más gordas y otras veces estás en cosas más humildes, pero para mí la pasión no es tampoco el set. La pasión es la construcción de algo que, en el momento en el que lo has construido, es efímero, pero tú eres el dueño de eso y queda ahí para la posteridad. KANDIDO. Los proyectos grandes o pequeños, con historias de gentes que tienen mucho que contar sean grandes o pequeñas, con personajes grandes y pequeños y que emocionan. PREGUNTA. ¿Qué les gustaría que el espectador se llevara consigo después de ver 'El triplete'? KARRA. Un buen momento. 'El triplete' no es un corto sesudo de estos que tengas que sacar una conclusión que te pueda aportar mucho en la vida, 'El triplete' es un divertimento. Yo creo que el espectador va a tener una buena aventura. Sobre todo es una oda a la amistad y una rebeldía desde la senectud. KANDIDO. Una sonrisa.

articles.title: Dani García, chef: "El truco para que el arroz quede más sabroso no está en el sofrito"
articles.standfirst: El chef Dani García explica cómo potenciar el sabor del arroz con una mezcla de cuatro especias
articles.summary: El chef Dani García explica cómo potenciar el sabor del arroz con una mezcla de cuatro especias
articles.body: Dani García tiene una forma diferente de entender los arroces. El chef marbellí, uno de los cocineros españoles más reconocidos internacionalmente, defiende que el sofrito no es imprescindible para conseguir un arroz sabroso y propone sustituirlo por una sencilla mezcla de especias. Una técnica que permite simplificar la preparación sin renunciar al sabor. La propuesta forma parte de la manera en la que García ha reinterpretado el arroz desde hace años. Según explica el cocinero, la idea comenzó a tomar forma en 2013, durante una estancia en un restaurante de Nueva York, cuando empezó a plantearse cómo trabajar el arroz fuera de los cánones tradicionales de la paella. La clave de su propuesta está en una combinación de "azafrán, clavo, pimienta negra y comino en polvo". El chef las utiliza trituradas y en proporciones equilibradas para aportar aroma y profundidad al arroz sin que las especias terminen ocultando el sabor del caldo o del propio cereal. "Mi truco para que el arroz quede más sabroso no es el sofrito, es esta mezcla de cuatro especias", explica García en la receta en la que desarrolla esta técnica. La propuesta rompe con una de las ideas más extendidas de la cocina doméstica española: que un buen arroz necesita necesariamente una base de verduras cocinadas lentamente. El chef no plantea, sin embargo, eliminar el resto de elementos importantes de la elaboración. En su receta utiliza un caldo de pollo de sabor relativamente suave, al que define como "elegante" y no excesivamente potente. La intención es que el arroz pueda absorber el sabor durante la cocción sin terminar resultando demasiado intenso. Otro de los trucos que utiliza García consiste en añadir un pequeño chorro de aceite al caldo. Según explica, esta técnica ayuda posteriormente a conseguir un socarrat suelto y crujiente. La ausencia de sofrito no significa, para el chef, renunciar a los elementos que considera fundamentales en un buen arroz. Entre ellos está precisamente el socarrat, la capa tostada que se forma en la parte inferior de la paella durante los últimos minutos de cocción. En una de sus elaboraciones, García prepara un arroz de chuleta utilizando arroz bomba, caldo de pollo y una chuleta de ternera. La carne se carameliza previamente por la parte de la grasa y esa grasa se convierte después en otro elemento para aportar sabor al arroz. La propuesta de Dani García permite así preparar un arroz con una estructura diferente a la de una paella tradicional, pero manteniendo algunos de sus elementos más reconocibles. La mezcla de especias funciona como sustituto aromático del sofrito y, además, permite reducir uno de los pasos más largos de este tipo de recetas: cocinar lentamente la base de verduras antes de incorporar el arroz y el caldo.

articles.title: 'La Revuelta' recibe a las campeonas del mundo de gimnasia rítmica entre reivindicaciones: "Lo que ganamos solo nos da para un coche"
articles.standfirst: David Broncano ha recibido al equipo español semanas después de hacerse con el oro
articles.summary: David Broncano ha recibido al equipo español semanas después de hacerse con el oro
articles.body: Convertirse en campeón o campeona del mundo en cualquier deporte no es un reto fácil. Sino, que se lo digan al equipo español de gimnasia rítmica que se hizo con el oro 35 años después. Un hito que ‘La Revuelta’ ha querido celebrar recibiendo a las componentes del combinado nacional. Inés Bergua, Salma Solaun, Andrea Fernández, Marina Cortelles, Andrea Corral y Lucía Muñoz fueron las invitadas al espacio presentado por David Broncano este miércoles, 16 de septiembre. Las españolas llegaban con el oro conquistado en el Campeonato del Mundo, celebrado en Frankfurt. Premio que se suma a los tres oros del pasado Campeonato de Europa de 2025, tres oros más en el Europeo de 2026 y un bronce en el Mundial de 2025. Lo que a priori puede parecer que equivale a un gran premio económico. Lejos de la realidad. Las gimnastas españolas denunciaron en el programa de Radio Televisión Española que, lo que para otros campeones puede servir para tener una economía saneada, a ellas solo les da para “comprarse un coche cada una”. “Nos sigue pareciendo insuficiente para ser campeonas del mundo y para todo lo que estamos haciendo. Ganamos muchísimo menos que cualquier otro campeón o campeona del mundo”, añadieron al hacer referencia a la beca que se les concederá en 2027 por el Mundial conquistado este año. Un logro que recobra más valor si se tiene en cuenta que para este mundial regresaron selecciones como Rusia o Bielorrusia, vetadas en el anterior por la guerra con Ucrania. Broncano se animó a mostrar sus dotes en la gimnasia rítmica participando en un ejercicio con el equipo al tener que cruzar por un aro. “Padeces el síndrome del azulejo: es más fácil partirte que doblarte”, le dijo una de ellas. “Claro, es que vosotras os tiráis todo el día entrenando”, contestó el presentador. A lo que las gimnastas le aclararon que suelen tener una rutina de “ocho horas o más al día porque son muchos ejercicios los que hay que aprender”: “A veces hasta que nos cierran el Centro de Alto Rendimiento (CAR)”. Candela Peña, colaboradora que apareció antes que ellas se quedó para recibirlas y elogiarlas. “No dejéis de entrenar que luego haces el pino puente y pareces una salchicha rajada en la parrilla y ya no podéis hacer ni el pino puente ni el spagat”. El equipo le regaló al presentador un cartel que emulaba al ticket que les da la clasificación directa a los Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028. Primeras españolas en conseguirlo. Además, le llevaron una pancarta enorme de una foto de ellas junto a Broncano, también con un moño en la cabeza, que rezaba: “Campeonas del mundo”.
